timeline_003: Choose an era to see what was happening — and where to find it in the museum.

timeline_eras.name: First villages
timeline_eras.summary: At Mehrgarh, in the hills west of the Indus, people grow wheat and barley, herd cattle and build mud-brick homes — among the earliest farming communities in South Asia.

timeline_eras.name: Indus–Sarasvati cities
timeline_eras.summary: Planned cities rise with grid streets, covered drains, great reservoirs and standard weights. Dholavira, in Gujarat, carefully managed every drop of water in a dry land.

timeline_eras.name: The Vedic age
timeline_eras.summary: The Vedas are composed and memorized with extraordinary precision, passed down orally for generations. Sanskrit becomes the language of ritual, philosophy and science.

timeline_eras.name: Seers, schools & science
timeline_eras.summary: Teachers question the nature of the self and the world. Mahavira and the Buddha found new paths, Panini writes a complete grammar of Sanskrit, and traditions of medicine take shape.
timeline_eras.keys: Panini · Mahavira · the Buddha · traditions of Sushruta and Charaka

timeline_eras.name: The classical age
timeline_eras.summary: Artisans carve and paint Ajanta. Aryabhata calculates the motions of the planets, and great centres of learning like Nalanda draw students from across Asia.

timeline_eras.name: The great temple builders
timeline_eras.summary: Builders carve the Kailasa temple at Ellora from a single rock, a queen commissions the Rani-ki-Vav stepwell, and the Sun Temple at Konark is built as a colossal stone chariot.

timeline_eras.name: The Bhakti movement
timeline_eras.summary: Poet-saints in every regional language sing of personal devotion to God, open to all regardless of birth. Their songs are still sung across India today.
timeline_eras.keys: Alvars and Nayanars · Mirabai · Tulsidas · Narsinh Mehta

timeline_eras.name: Bhagwan Swaminarayan
timeline_eras.summary: Born in Chhapaiya, he travels across India before settling in Gujarat, teaching devotion and moral living, building mandirs and leading social reform.

timeline_eras.name: A global family
timeline_eras.summary: Hindu traditions travel with families to every continent. BAPS has built over 1,200 mandirs worldwide, and in 2023 Akshardham opened in Robbinsville, New Jersey.
